subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general internal-warning destination/category router under messages, and what categories/defaults should it support relative to existing suppression and cron failure destinations?
rationale: The implementation shape changes public config and warning-delivery semantics across gateway, agent, cron, and channel surfaces; code inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Approve default-compatible router
options.body: Add a documented explicit-opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

options.title: Keep suppression-only policy
options.body: Treat messages.suppressToolErrors and cron.failureDestination as the supported operator controls and narrow this issue to docs or channel-specific leaks.

options.title: Split by warning class
options.body: Defer a general router and handle lifecycle, tool errors, and cron notifications as separate narrowly owned issues.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible router
recommendation.body: Add a documented explicit-opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently authored and merged adjacent warning-delivery behavior and are the strongest routing candidate among the inspected history.
